subject: Human Body
title: Immunotherapy Against Cancer
description: A quick win: understand Immunotherapy Against Cancer.

hook.text: What if you could train your own immune system to hunt and destroy cancer cells? That's immunotherapy.

buildup.text: Checkpoint inhibitors are drugs that remove the 'brakes' cancer puts on T cells. Freed T cells attack tumors.

discovery.text: CAR-T therapy genetically engineers a patient's own T cells to recognize cancer.

twist.text: Immunotherapy doesn't work for every cancer. Some tumors hide too well or suppress immune responses too effectively.

climax.text: Immunotherapy harnesses the body's own defenses against cancer. It's not a cure-all, but it's rewriting oncology.

punchline.text: The best cancer fighter might be your own immune system.

quiz.question: What do checkpoint inhibitors do?
options: They directly kill cancer cells with chemicals
They remove the brakes cancer puts on T cells
They prevent cancer cells from dividing
